deep.reconstruction:
Heading dated July–August 1967: 'Anneaux (co)simpliciaux canoniques et modules stratifiés'. A bracketed note says the development is formally independent of the theories of crystalline or stratifying sites. So Grothendieck wants a purely algebraic, Čech-type approach to stratifications that does not go through the infinitesimal or crystalline topos.

Section 1:
- Let X → S be a relative prescheme (the image reads more like 'relatif' than 'lisse').
- For n ≥ 0 put X^{[n]} = X ×_S ... ×_S X, with n+1 factors. View it as an object of (Sch)/S together with the diagonal immersion X → X^{[n]}.
- Let \hat{X}^{[n]} be the formal completion of X^{[n]} along the diagonal.
- As n varies, the \hat{X}^{[n]} form a simplicial formal scheme. This is the Čech nerve of X → S completed along the diagonal; in modern terms, the formal groupoid of X/S (the infinitesimal or de Rham groupoid), whose 'quotient' is the de Rham stack.
- All the underlying spaces equal esp(X). So the structure sheaves P^n can be placed on the single space |X|. Each P^n is an ℕ-indexed pro-object (the system of n-th order infinitesimal neighbourhoods), i.e. a ring object of Pro(Ann(Esp(X))), the pro-category of sheaves of rings on |X|.
- As n varies one obtains a cosimplicial Ring P^* on |X| with P^0 = O_X. P^1 is the completed sheaf of principal parts lim P^m_{X/S}.
- The page breaks off at 'Faisons attention que certaines...'. The next page completes the warning: the two coface maps O_X ⇉ P^1 differ, so P^1 carries two distinct O_X-algebra structures.
- The next page then introduces the shifted (décalé) object (SP)^i = P^{i+1} with α: P^* → SP^*. In the affine case Γ(P^i) is the completed tensor power A^{⊗(i+1)}.

Purpose: set up the canonical cosimplicial ring (Čech–Alexander or Amitsur-type object) so that stratified modules can be defined as cosimplicial P^*-modules, i.e. descent data with respect to the formal groupoid. De Rham or infinitesimal cohomology would then be computed by the associated cosimplicial complex, without sites.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page.

The formal completion along the diagonal requires the diagonal X → X^{[n]} to be an immersion (e.g. X separated, or at least locally separated). The page does not state this, but the next page adds it explicitly.

The page does not yet say that P^* is only a cosimplicial sheaf of rings, not a cosimplicial O_X-algebra, because the coface maps from P^0 differ. The sentence is cut off precisely where Grothendieck begins this caveat, and the next page completes it.

ideas.what: Simplicial formal scheme obtained by completing the Čech nerve X^{[n]} = X^{×_S (n+1)} along the diagonal; the formal groupoid of X/S
ideas.modern_name: Infinitesimal (formal) groupoid / completed Čech nerve; formal model of the de Rham stack X_dR
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck, 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (IHES 1966, publ. Dix exposés 1968); developed by Berthelot (1974) and Berthelot–Ogus (1978); de Rham stack by Simpson (1996)
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas, 1968), sections on stratifications and the formal completion of the diagonal; EGA IV 16 for principal parts

ideas.what: Structure sheaves of the completed nerve, all living on |X|, viewed as an ℕ-pro-object of sheaves of rings and forming a cosimplicial Ring P^* with P^0 = O_X
ideas.modern_name: Cosimplicial ring of (completed) principal parts; Čech–Alexander / Amitsur complex for the de Rham (infinitesimal) groupoid
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (principal parts, EGA IV 16; Crystals 1966–68); the Čech–Alexander complex as used by Berthelot–Ogus and Bhatt–de Jong

ideas.what: Programme: define stratified modules (HPD/infinitesimal stratifications) as cosimplicial modules over P^*, independently of crystalline or stratifying sites
ideas.modern_name: Stratifications = descent data along the formal groupoid = crystals in O_{X/S}-modules (infinitesimal); comodules over the Hopf algebroid P^1
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes, §2 (stratifications)

deep.surprise_reason: This is the standard setup of the formal groupoid and the cosimplicial ring of principal parts. It already appears in Grothendieck's 1966 IHES crystals lectures and in EGA IV 16, and was later systematised by Berthelot. The emphasis on a site-free, purely cosimplicial treatment is a mild point of methodological interest. It anticipates the later Čech–Alexander / de Rham-stack viewpoint, but that viewpoint is well represented in the literature.
transcription_corrections: Title: the crossed-out word before 'simpliciaux' appears to be a false start; the title may read 'Anneaux co-simpliciaux canoniques'. This would be consistent with P^* being cosimplicial, but it is uncertain.
'un préschéma lisse[?]' more likely reads 'un préschéma relatif'.
'Sch f/X' should probably be 'Schf/S' (category of formal preschemes over S), in 'on trouve un objet simplicial de ... Schf/S'.
'AN-pro-objet' should read 'ℕ-pro-objet' (pro-object indexed by the natural numbers).
'sur Inf[?](X)' (twice) should read 'sur esp(X)' (the underlying space of X), consistent with 'les espaces sous-jacents ... égaux à esp(X)'.
The ring category reads 'Pro(Ann(Esp(X)))' or 'Pro(Ann(esp(X)))': the pro-category of sheaves of rings on the space of X.
